title: Unauthorized disclosure of continuous health and location data
description: The wearable device continuously captures sensitive personal data (heart rate, GPS position, timestamps) which could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through device compromise, data leaks, or insecure transmission to cloud services.
assumptions: Assumes device may be compromised or data transmitted without adequate encryption

title: Unauthorized access to device and stored sensor data
description: The wearable device may be vulnerable to unauthorized access by attackers who could extract, modify, or intercept the continuous sensor telemetry data being captured.
assumptions: Assumes device has authentication mechanisms that may be bypassed or weak

title: Unintended consequences of continuous location and health tracking
description: Continuous monitoring of GPS position and health metrics may lead to unintended surveillance, stalking, or profiling of the user without their explicit consent or awareness.
assumptions: Assumes user may not be fully aware of all data collection activities

title: Loss of sensitive health and location data during transmission
description: Sensor telemetry data transmitted from the wearable device may be lost or corrupted during transmission to cloud services or other destinations, potentially resulting in incomplete or inaccurate health records.
assumptions: Assumes transmission may occur over networks with potential packet loss or interference

title: Unintended Data Disclosure to Companion App
description: Personal data (exercise sessions, GPS traces, device ID, timestamps) is transferred from wearable device to companion app. While this is an explicit disclosure by design, there is risk that data may be disclosed to third parties through the companion app or that the minimality principle is not being followed (collecting more data than strictly required).

title: User unawareness of data sharing
description: User may not be aware that their calorie, meal, and weight data entered into the companion app could be shared with third parties, used for advertising, or sold to data brokers beyond the app's intended purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the app collects and potentially shares user health data

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health data
description: User's sensitive health data (calories, meals, weight) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through app vulnerabilities, data breaches, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Assumes the app stores and transmits user health data

title: Data loss during entry or transmission
description: User's manually entered calorie, meal, and weight data could be lost during entry, transmission to the app, or storage within the companion mobile app.
assumptions: Assumes the app processes and stores user health data

title: Unintended Location Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: GPS location traces stored in DS2 may be accessed or shared with third parties without user consent, violating privacy principles. Location data is highly sensitive personal data that could be used for profiling, surveillance, or other unauthorized purposes.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The app may collect more location data than strictly necessary for its intended function, violating the minimality principle. Continuous GPS tracking may be more intrusive than required for typical location history features.

title: Implicit Location Data Disclosure Through Metadata
description: Location data stored in DS2 may be disclosed implicitly through metadata or derived from other disclosed data, even if the primary data itself is not directly shared.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: The location history store DS2 may be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of sensitive location data. Access controls and authentication mechanisms may be insufficient.

title: Data Breach Leading to Location Data Exposure
description: A security breach of DS2 could result in exposure of stored location traces, potentially enabling tracking, profiling, or other privacy violations.

title: Health Data Disclosure to Analytics Service
description: Personal health data (calorie, weight, exercise logs) is transferred from Health Log Store to Analytics Service for health-condition analysis. This represents an explicit data disclosure by design, but there is risk of implicit disclosure if the analytics service shares data with third parties or if the transfer is not properly controlled.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: The analytics service may collect more personal health data than strictly required for health-condition analysis, violating the minimality principle. Calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions may include unnecessary personal identifiers or derived health metrics.

title: Data Sharing with Third Parties
description: The Health Analytics Service may share the processed health data with third parties (e.g., insurance companies, researchers, advertisers) without explicit consent, leading to unintended data disclosure.

title: Information Leakage During Data Processing
description: During health-condition analysis, the analytics service may inadvertently leak personal health information through metadata, error messages, or derived health metrics that could be used to infer sensitive information about individuals.

title: Unauthorized Access to Health Data
description: The Health Analytics Service may be compromised or accessed by unauthorized personnel, leading to unauthorized access to personal health data stored in the Health Log Store.

title: Profiling of health condition patterns
description: The Health Analytics Service infers health-condition risk indicators and trend flags that could be used to profile individuals or groups based on their health data patterns, potentially leading to unwanted inferences about health status.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics service has access to sufficient health data to generate meaningful patterns.

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management for health analytics data
description: The transmission of inferred health insights from the Analytics Service to the Companion App may lack adequate cybersecurity risk management measures, potentially exposing sensitive health information to unauthorized access or interception.
assumptions: Assumes health analytics data contains sensitive personal information requiring proper security controls.

title: Inference of individual health status from aggregated insights
description: The Companion Mobile App may infer or deduce individual health status from the received health-condition risk indicators and trend flags, potentially leading to unwanted identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Assumes the app processes the received insights in a way that could identify or infer individual health conditions.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health indicators
description: The app dashboard displays inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals to the user. If the user is not aware that their data is being displayed or if there's unauthorized access to this information, sensitive health data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: User may not be fully aware of what data is being displayed or how it's being used

title: User unawareness of data display and usage
description: Users may not be aware that their health-related data is being displayed on the dashboard or how it's being used for inference. This lack of awareness could lead to privacy concerns and reduced trust in the application.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into what data is being processed and displayed

title: Identification of individuals through health indicators
description: The displayed eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals could potentially identify individuals, especially when combined with other data. This could lead to unwanted identification or profiling of users.
assumptions: Health indicators may be unique enough to identify individuals when combined with other data

title: Non-compliance with health data protection regulations
description: Displaying inferred health condition indicators may not be in full compliance with applicable health data protection regulations, standards, and best practices. This could lead to legal and organizational risk.
assumptions: There may be gaps in compliance with health data protection regulations

title: Unnecessary transfer of health and location data to third-party cloud provider
description: The Health Analytics Service transfers full health and location datasets to the Cloud Hosting Provider. This explicit disclosure of personal data to a third party may violate the minimality principle if the data is not strictly required for the intended purpose. The transfer of complete datasets rather than only necessary subsets increases privacy risk.
assumptions: The cloud provider is a third party outside the system boundary and may have different security and privacy standards.

title: Potential information leakage during data transfer to cloud provider
description: During the transfer of analytics data, models, and health/location datasets to the Cloud Hosting Provider, there is a risk of data interception, unauthorized access, or leakage during transmission. This could expose sensitive personal information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The transfer occurs over a network and may be subject to interception or unauthorized access.

title: Unintended disclosure through metadata or derived data
description: The transfer of health and location datasets to the cloud provider may result in unintended disclosures through metadata, derived information, or incidental data that could be used to infer sensitive personal information beyond the explicitly disclosed data.
assumptions: Metadata and derived data from the transferred datasets may contain sensitive information.
